title: What If Earth Orbited Two Suns?

scenes.text: What if Earth had two suns? Real planets already do, and sunsets there come in pairs.
Kepler-16b, about 200 light-years away, circles two stars every 229 days.
Both stars are smaller than ours, with about 69 percent and 20 percent of the Sun's mass.
Habitable zones shift. An Earth-size world might need to sit near twice our distance, wrapped in greenhouse gases.
Kepler-1647b is a giant sitting in its habitable zone, taking 1,107 days to orbit both stars.
By 2016, astronomers had confirmed eleven such planets. Two sunsets may be common.

description:
What if Earth orbited two suns?
Real planets circle two stars, and some sit where liquid water could exist.
